sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let's learn how to create methods in Java - your code's superheroes! Methods help you organize and reuse code like LEGO blocks.

• What methods are and why they're useful
• How to define your own methods
• The basic structure of a method
• How to call methods to make them work

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine methods as little robots that do specific jobs for you. Need to calculate something? There's a robot for that. Need to display a message? Another robot!

Methods are like these robots - they:
• Have a specific job to do
• Can be called whenever you need that job done
• Can take inputs and give outputs

Here's the simplest method structure:
```java
public static void methodName() {
    // Code to execute
}
```
• `public static` - We'll learn these later (just include them for now)
• `void` - Means the method doesn't return anything
• `methodName()` - Your custom name for the method
• `{}` - The method's code goes between these braces

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Defining a Method works:

steps.title: Define the Method
steps.description: First, we create our method (our little robot) with a specific job - in this case, saying hello.

steps.title: Call the Method
steps.description: Now we tell our robot to do its job by calling its name. The method runs and prints "Hello!".

steps.title: See the Result
steps.description: When we run the program, it executes the main method which calls sayHello(), and we see the output.
steps.code:
Hello!
// This is what appears in the console

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Methods are blocks of code that perform specific tasks
✓ They help organize code and avoid repetition
✓ Method definition includes: modifiers, return type, name, and body
✓ You call a method by using its name followed by parentheses
✓ Every Java program starts with the main method

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Give methods descriptive names (like calculateTax instead of calc)
Keep methods small - one job per method
Use consistent naming (camelCase for method names)
donts: Don't create methods that do too many things
Don't forget the parentheses when calling methods
Don't mix up method definition and method call
sections.protip: Start with simple methods that do one thing well - you can always combine them later!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Defining a Method used in real apps?

examples.how: Methods calculate interest, validate transactions, and generate account statements
Methods handle player movement, collision detection, and scoring systems
Methods process payments, apply discounts, and calculate shipping costs

problem.description: Create a method called printGreeting that prints "Welcome to Java Programming!" to the console. Then call this method from your main method.
hints: Remember the basic method structure: public static void methodName()
Don't forget the curly braces {} for the method body
Call the method by writing its name followed by ()
problem.explanation: We defined printGreeting() to print our message, then called it from main(). When the program runs, main() executes first and calls our method, which prints the greeting.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Methods are reusable blocks of code that perform specific tasks
📌 Every method has a name, body, and can be called when needed
📌 Practice defining and calling simple methods to build confidence
📌 You're now ready to learn about method parameters and return values!
